conventions: Run prep, embedded in every eval prompt: copy the named fixture context repo into <run-dir>/outputs/<repo-name>/, `git init` the copy, `git config user.name "<fixture person display name>" && git config user.email "<fixture person email>"`, stage every fixture file including dotfiles, commit as `fixture baseline`, then operate with the copy as cwd. Before acting, save a sorted SHA-256 manifest of every copied fixture file outside `.git/`, the exact HEAD, and `git status --short` outside the copied repo; repeat all three after acting. Use only the copied repo and run directory. Never read or write ~/.gtm, any real context repo, home-directory config, or any path outside <run-dir>, except the explicitly supplied skill and fixture source paths. Never create machine state, registries, pins, or state files. Every eval has complete inputs and an empty `user_replies` array: any assistant question or approval gate is an automatic contractual failure. Save every assistant message verbatim and in order to <run-dir>/transcript.md; after any platform skill-use notice, `Sources read:` must be the first workflow content, and the position echo must precede any preliminary or final classification. Record every shell command verbatim in <run-dir>/command-log.txt; any Git inspection must use `git -C <repo-root>`. Keep all run evidence outside the copied context repo. Baseline arms must not invoke or consult any installed skill; with-skill arms may use the supplied gtm-lead-segmentation skill and installed siblings. Eval dirs are named eval-<ID>-<descriptive-name>, with outputs in run-1/outputs/. These harness requirements live only here, never in shipping SKILL.md.

evals.prompt: I’m at the root of our Gridline GTM context repo. Segment Alex Morgan at ForgeOne against the visible personas. Supplied facts only: title `Director of Revenue Systems`; internal employee; owns CRM architecture, lead routing, and the forecasting cadence. We do not know whether Alex is the executive sponsor. Return exactly one existing qualified persona label or `no-match` with every fixed one-off and metadata field. Responsibilities must outrank title. Ask no questions, do not browse or enrich, and write nothing.
evals.expected_output: A question-free response beginning its workflow content with Sources read, whose working line precedes classification, assigns exactly revenue-operations-leader with high confidence and needs_review false because supplied responsibilities are decisive, retains unknown executive sponsorship as an open question rather than review, and explicitly reports no side effects. Fixture bytes, HEAD, and clean status remain unchanged.
expectations: O1-O3 exact fields, label, rationale, and lead-level calibration

evals.prompt:
I’m at the root of our Veridian GTM context repo. Segment these contacts against visible personas using supplied facts only. Ask zero questions, do not browse or enrich, and write nothing.

| lead | company | title | supplied facts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nina Karlsson | NordPay | Head of Fraud Operations | internal employee; owns 28 investigators, queue policy, analyst capacity, and case tooling |
| Omar Haddad | Beacon Bank | Chief Compliance Officer | internal executive; owns AML policy, regulatory remediation, and compliance budget |
| Owen Hart | Hart Advisory | Fraud Advisor | external advisor serving three clients; no internal operating authority |
| Priya Shah | Kestrel | VP Risk | title only; employment type and responsibilities not supplied |

Start with the fixed bulk summary, then return every lead once using the fixed literal columns and metadata fields. Return one exact visible qualified label or `no-match` per lead. Confidence and `needs_review` must reflect each lead’s evidence gaps rather than any persona maintenance backlog.
evals.expected_output: A question-free bulk response beginning with counts fraud-operations-leader 1, compliance-executive 1, no-match 2, low-confidence 1, review-needed 1, plus common evidence and questions. Nina and Omar match their exact personas; Owen is a high-confidence no-match with no review due to the external-advisor disqualifier; Priya is the only low-confidence needs_review row. Every row and metadata field is present; no side effects occur.
expectations: B1-B5 exact summary order, columns, counts, labels, and lead-level calibration

evals.prompt: I’m in the `emea` child of our Cloudmason GTM context repo. Segment Lea Novak at Baltic Ledger against the personas visible here. Supplied facts only: title `Director of Cloud Security, EMEA`; internal employee; owns regional cloud-security controls, security engineering, and cloud-risk posture; explicitly does not own the DORA remediation program. Respect nearest same-stem precedence and retain non-colliding inherited personas. Return exactly one existing qualified persona label or `no-match` with every fixed one-off and metadata field. Ask no questions, do not browse or enrich, and make no changes.
evals.expected_output: A question-free child-position response that reports root and child org sources; reports root security-leader as overridden by child security-leader while inherited procurement-executive and child dora-program-owner remain visible; assigns exactly emea/security-leader and rejects emea/dora-program-owner on supplied non-ownership; uses high confidence and needs_review false; and explicitly reports no side effects.
expectations: P1-P3 exact child visibility, supplied-evidence rejection, label, and calibration
